title: Engine: the body always faces the crosshair; interaction uses the eye-plane ray
player_outcome: In third person the body always faces where the crosshair points: A/D strafes and S backpedals with the torso on target. Bushes or trees behind the player never become the target, so the player no longer swings or mines backwards. Close blocks no longer twist the body sideways.
design: InteractionController.UpdateTarget, reach and filter: reach = ItemUseSystem.ReachMeters(Entity, held.Item); filter = ItemUseSystem.FilterFor(held info).
UpdateTarget, target: Target = Targeting.CastView(world, cam, dir, Entity.Eye, reach + 2, filter, out startT); InReach = Target.Distance <= reach.
UpdateTarget, convergence: a second Targeting.CastView(..., 60 m, TargetFilter.None) gives the crosshair world point (terrain or 60 m).
UpdateTarget, entity fields: Entity.ViewDirection = dir; Entity.Aim = Normalize(point - Eye); Entity.AimDistance = |point - Eye|. DigDownTarget is unchanged.
InteractionController.UpdateTalkTarget: skip residents with along < startT (interim; P1-07 replaces this with entity picking).
PlayerAvatar.Motion.Animate: facing yaw = _controller.Rig.Yaw (never the aim vector); the non-humanoid branch also uses the facing.
PlayerAvatar.Motion, rewrite TurnLegs(facing, v, ground, upright, alive, dt). Idle: target = facing, eased at rate 12/s, with no 55° hysteresis. Upright (air, swim, rope): facing.

TurnLegs, moving: rel = AngleDifference(facing, moveYaw). If |rel| <= 100° then legs = facing + Clamp(rel, ±45°) with a forward gait (A/D strafe). Else legs = facing + Clamp(AngleDifference(facing, move + π), ±45°) with _backwards = true.
AimModifier.Twist = AngleDifference(_legYaw, facing), always within 45°. Pitch stays from Aim.
PlayerAvatar: expose float FacingErrorDegrees = |AngleDifference(_legYaw + twist, facing)| in degrees.
LaunchedWorld: add PlayerAvatar? Avatar; WorldLauncher fills it.
GodotCommandHost probes: target.front (1 if Target is null or Dot(targetPoint - Eye, Facing) > 0), target.dist (Target?.Distance ?? -1), avatar.facing_error.
docs/architecture/gameplay.md: document the view ray, filters and facing rule.
files_modify: game/Player/InteractionController.cs — CastView targeting, convergence cast, ViewDirection/Aim/AimDistance, reach helper
game/Player/PlayerAvatar.Motion.cs — facing = camera yaw, strafe/backpedal legs, FacingErrorDegrees
tests: combat.cmds, after the arena setup: 'camera third' / 'wield copper_pickaxe' / 'fill -2 0 6 2 5 6 stone' / 'aim 0 0 1' / 'wait 0.3' / 'assert target.front == 1' / 'assert target.dist > 2' / 'assert avatar.facing_error < 5' / 'hold move_left 0.6' / 'assert avatar.facing_error < 5' / 'hold move_back 0.6' / 'assert avatar.facing_error < 5' / 'fill -2 0 6 2 5 6 air'
Core TargetingTests (P1-05) carry the behind-the-player logic
verification: Headless smoke combat.cmds and basic.cmds PASS
Manual third person: stand with a bush or tree right behind; the highlight and dig always land in front
Strafe with A/D and backpedal with S while aiming: the torso stays on the crosshair and the legs step sideways or backwards; mining a block right beside the right shoulder no longer spins the body
lavapipe animation.cmds l_strafe and j_run shots look natural
risks: Clamping leg offset to 45° while strafing at 90° gives a crab-walk; tune the 45°/100° constants from the l_strafe screenshot.
The convergence cast adds one extra DDA of at most 120 cells per tick (negligible).
Hook and minecart facing paths were aim-based before; check the minecart ride visually.
